question: In which plant tissue does photosynthesis mainly occur?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mesophyll**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mesophyll** tissue is the primary site for photosynthesis in plants.
 
• It is located within the leaves, specifically in the palisade and spongy layers.
 
• The palisade mesophyll cells are elongated and contain numerous chloroplasts, making them highly efficient at capturing light energy.
 
• The spongy mesophyll cells have a looser arrangement, facilitating gas exchange.
 
• Photosynthesis involves the conversion of light energy into chemical energy, producing glucose and oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chloroplasts** are the organelles within mesophyll cells where photosynthesis takes place.
 
• The **leaf structure** is adapted to maximize the efficiency of photosynthesis, with a large surface area and specialized cells.
 
• The **stomata** on the leaf surface control the exchange of gases, such as carbon dioxide and oxygen, which are essential for photosynthesis.
 
• Water and minerals necessary for photosynthesis are transported to the leaves through the **xylem** tissue.
 
• The **phloem** tissue distributes the produced glucose to other parts of the plant for growth and storage.
